notes: Human-readable descriptions of every router-supported capability in agents.json. The goal decomposer uses this as a catalog_hint so the LLM can REUSE these slugs instead of coining synonymous ones (which discovery scouts can't match). Each entry is the LLM's only signal for what a slug means — keep `description` precise and `examples` concrete. When you add a new capability to agents.json, you MUST add a matching entry here or the decomposer will silently coin a synonym.

calendar_management.description: Read, create, update, or cancel calendar events; manage meeting invites, attendee responses, and availability lookups across calendar systems like Google Calendar, Outlook, or Calendly.
examples: Schedule a meeting with three teammates next Tuesday
Find a 30-minute slot when everyone on the team is free
Cancel all recurring meetings for someone on leave

code_review.description: Review source code diffs, pull requests, or whole files for correctness, style, security, or maintainability issues, returning structured comments or a verdict.
examples: Review this pull request for security issues
Suggest improvements to a function
Flag style violations in a commit

code_search.description: Search source code repositories by symbol name, function signature, regex, or natural-language intent across one or many repos. NOT for general web search.
examples: Find every call site of `parseUser` in the org's repos
Show how a specific React hook is used across the codebase
Locate the SQL migration that added the `users` table

company_data_lookup.description: Given a company name or domain, look up firmographic data: headquarters, employee count, industry, funding rounds, exec roster, parent/subsidiary structure.
examples: Get the headcount and funding history for Acme Corp
Find the CEO and CTO of a private company
Look up which industry vertical a vendor is in

contact_enrichment.description: Given a partial contact (name, email, or company), find verified contact details: corporate email, phone, LinkedIn URL, role, employer. Person-level enrichment, not company-level.
examples: Find the work email for Jane Smith at Acme
Resolve a LinkedIn profile to a phone number
Look up the title of someone given just their email

crm_query.description: Read or write records in a hosted CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, etc.): query opportunities, accounts, contacts, tasks, notes; create or update them.
examples: Pull the last 10 opportunities for an account in Salesforce
Create a new lead in HubSpot
Update the stage of a deal in Pipedrive

customer_support_lookup.description: Search a vendor's support knowledge base, FAQ, help-center articles, or ticket history to answer how-to or status questions.
examples: Find the help article explaining how to enable SSO
Look up the resolution of a previous support ticket
Search the FAQ for refund policy

data_visualization.description: Render charts, graphs, dashboards, or interactive visualisations from structured input data (CSV, JSON, SQL result set). Produces images, HTML, or chart configs.
examples: Make a bar chart of monthly revenue
Build a dashboard showing user signups by region
Generate a line graph from a CSV

email_send.description: Send an email (transactional or marketing) via SMTP or a hosted API like Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, AWS SES.
examples: Send a confirmation email to a customer
Email a daily summary to a distribution list
Send a one-off notification to an address

email_verification.description: Given an email address, determine whether it is deliverable: catch-all detection, MX validity, syntax, role-account flag, disposable-domain check. Pre-send hygiene only.
examples: Check whether `jane@acme.com` is a valid mailbox
Filter a list of leads to drop bouncing addresses
Detect whether an address is a disposable inbox

file_operations.description: Read, write, list, move, copy, or delete files on local disk or in cloud object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Dropbox). For programmatic file manipulation, not document understanding.
examples: Upload a file to an S3 bucket
List all files in a Google Drive folder
Move a folder from one location to another

general_research.description: Open-ended web research that synthesises information from multiple sources into a written report. Use when the task needs reading and summarising several pages, not a single answer.
examples: Research the top 5 e-bike brands in India and write a comparison
Investigate the regulatory landscape for stablecoins in the EU
Summarise the academic literature on a topic

image_generation.description: Generate images from text prompts via models like DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, Imagen. Produces image files or URLs.
examples: Create a logo for a new product
Generate a header image for a blog post
Make a stylised portrait from a description

legal_document_review.description: Analyse legal documents (contracts, NDAs, policies, terms of service) for risky clauses, missing provisions, deviations from standard templates, or compliance issues.
examples: Flag risky clauses in this vendor contract
Check whether an NDA matches our template
Review a privacy policy for GDPR compliance

ocr.description: Extract text from images or scanned PDFs (printed or handwritten). Optical character recognition only — not document layout understanding or form parsing.
examples: Extract the text from a scanned invoice image
Read the printed text on a photograph
Convert a scanned PDF into searchable text

payment_authorization.description: Initiate or authorise a payment, create a charge, capture an authorised charge, or issue a refund via a payments processor (Stripe, Razorpay, PayPal, Adyen). Use this for ANY 'buy', 'purchase', 'checkout', 'pay for', 'collect payment' style sub-task.
examples: Charge a customer's card for $50
Authorise a payment for an e-commerce order
Issue a refund for a returned product
Process the checkout step for a purchase

price_comparison.description: Compare prices for the same product, service, or SKU across multiple vendors, marketplaces, or quote APIs. Use this for ANY 'compare prices', 'find the cheapest', 'filter by budget' style sub-task.
examples: Find the cheapest seller for an iPhone in India
Compare hotel prices across three booking sites
Filter products in a category by price range

semantic_search.description: Search a corpus (documents, embeddings index, vector database) by meaning rather than keywords. Returns ranked passages from the supplied corpus, not the open web.
examples: Find documents in our knowledge base similar to a question
Retrieve the most relevant FAQ entries for a query
Look up internal docs by intent rather than exact words

shipping_quote.description: Get shipping rates, delivery time estimates, or carrier options for sending a package from an origin address to a destination via UPS, FedEx, USPS, Shippo, ShipEngine, Delhivery, Bluedart. Use this for 'arrange delivery', 'estimate shipping', 'pick a courier' style sub-tasks.
examples: Get a UPS quote to ship a 2 kg package from Bengaluru to Mumbai
Compare carrier options for international shipping
Estimate delivery time for a domestic package

store_locator.description: Find brick-and-mortar store locations for a brand or category near a city, postcode, or coordinates. Returns store addresses, hours, contact info. Geography-aware, not general search.
examples: Find Apple stores in Bengaluru
List the nearest pharmacies to a postcode
Look up showrooms for a car brand in a city

text_summarization.description: Condense a long passage of text into a shorter summary at a specified length or detail level. Single-document, not a research synthesis across many sources.
examples: Summarise a 20-page report into 5 bullet points
Write a TL;DR for a long article
Reduce a meeting transcript to key decisions

transcription.description: Convert spoken audio (recorded or live) into written text. Use for podcasts, meetings, voice notes, calls. Audio-to-text only.
examples: Transcribe a Zoom recording
Convert a voicemail to text
Get a written transcript of a podcast episode

translation.description: Translate text from one human language to another (e.g. English to Hindi, Japanese to French). Whole-passage translation, not glossary lookups.
examples: Translate a product description from English to German
Translate a support reply into Spanish
Localise marketing copy into Japanese

web_browsing.description: Drive a real browser to navigate to URLs, click buttons, fill forms, scroll, and read the rendered DOM. Use when JavaScript-driven sites or login walls block plain HTTP fetches, or when a multi-step interactive workflow is required.
examples: Log into a portal and download a report
Fill out a multi-page web form
Click through a checkout flow that requires JavaScript

web_scraping.description: Fetch a web page and extract structured data (lists, tables, fields) from its HTML. Single-page or list-of-pages extraction, no interaction beyond the initial fetch. Use for documentation, product pages, news sites.
examples: Extract product prices and titles from a category page
Scrape the news headlines from a public homepage
Pull structured fields from a documentation page

web_search.description: Query a general-purpose web search engine (Google, Bing, Brave, Tavily, Exa) and return ranked results. Use this for ANY 'find X on the web', 'research options', 'look up ideas', 'search for vendors', 'discover products' style sub-task. This is the default tool for open-web information gathering when no more specific capability fits.
examples: Find gift ideas for a 3-year-old
Look up vendors that sell a specific product
Search for reviews of a product or brand
Discover popular options in a category
Research what's available in a market
